# spotlight_hook (Resource)

A hook a team has defined: steps Spotlight takes whenever an event it fires `on` matches, each calling a tool an integration offers or sending a request. Write each expression in a step as `$${{ ... }}`, and `when` bare; `terraform plan` type-checks every one where it is written. Import it as `<workspace id>/<team key>/<key>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "random_password" "hook" {
  length  = 32
  special = false
}

# Whenever an agent searches Grafana, tell the team in Slack and keep an audit trail.
resource "spotlight_hook" "grafana_reads" {
  team_id = spotlight_team.core.id
  key     = "grafana-reads"
  on      = "tool.used"
  match = {
    # A tool renamed or removed in the integration fails the plan here.
    tools = [spotlight_integration.grafana.tools["search"]]
  }
  # when is bare CEL; plan type-checks it.
  when = "event.inputs.query != ''"
  steps = [
    {
      name = "notify"
      call = spotlight_integration.slack.tools["post-message"]
      with = {
        channel = "C024BE91L"
        # $${{ }} keeps the expression from Terraform; plan type-checks it.
        text = "Agent searched Grafana: $${{ event.inputs.query }}"
      }
    },
    {
      name = "audit"
      request = {
        url = aws_lambda_function_url.audit.function_url
      }
    },
  ]
  signing = {
    secret_wo         = "whsec_${base64encode(random_password.hook.result)}"
    secret_wo_version = 1
  }
}

# Hold back a pull request that touches the migrations until a DBA's endpoint lets it open.
resource "spotlight_hook" "migrations" {
  team_id = spotlight_team.core.id
  key     = "migrations-need-a-dba"
  on      = "pull-request.opening"
  match = {
    paths = ["db/migrations/**"]
  }
  vars = { migrations = "db/migrations/" }
  steps = [
    {
      name = "review"
      request = {
        url  = "https://dba.acme.dev/review"
        body = "$${{ {'pr': event.title, 'files': event.changed.filter(path, path.startsWith(vars.migrations))} }}"
      }
    },
  ]
  signing = {
    oidc = { audience = "https://dba.acme.dev" }
  }
  failure         = "block"
  timeout_seconds = 20
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Names the hook within its team, as in `migrations-need-a-dba`. It is fixed for the hook's life, so changing it replaces the hook.
- `on` (String) The event the hook fires on: `tool.using`, `tool.used`, `run.starting`, `run.ended`, `handover.giving`, `pull-request.opening`, `pull-request.merged`, `task.opened`, `task.moved`. The `.using`, `.starting`, `.giving` and `.opening` events fire before what they name, so a hook on one may stop it.
- `steps` (Dynamic) What the hook does, in order: a list of at least one step, each an object that either calls a tool or sends a request. Every step has a `name`, lowercase words joined by dashes, by which later steps read its outcome as `step.<name>`. A step that calls a tool names it in `call`, as in `spotlight_integration.slack.tools["post-message"]`, and gives it its inputs in `with`, an object of any JSON. A step that sends a request sets `request`: its `url`, any `headers` beside the ones Spotlight signs with, its `body`, which is any JSON and, left out, is the event, task and run, and `from`: `spotlight`, the default, to send it from Spotlight, to a host the control plane's `OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS` allows, or `network`, to have a host of the workspace send it from inside its network. A hook that sends a request signs it, so it needs `signing`. Strings in `with`, and a request's `url`, `headers` and `body`, may hold `$${{ ... }}` expressions, which read what `when` does and `step`.
- `team_id` (String) The team the hook belongs to. Changing it replaces the hook.

### Optional

- `failure` (String) What a failed step does to the event: `continue` lets it go on; `block` stops it, which only an event that fires before what it names can be.
- `match` (Attributes) Narrows the events the hook fires on; each list left out or empty narrows nothing. Left out, the hook fires on every event it is `on`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--match))
- `signing` (Attributes) How the hook signs the requests its steps send: with the HMAC secret `secret_wo`, as Standard Webhooks sign, or with an OIDC token for an `oidc` audience. Needed by a hook with a step that sends a request; a hook whose steps only call tools leaves it out. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--signing))
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) How many seconds each request may take, and a hook that fires before an event as a whole, from 1 to 30.
- `vars` (Map of String) Values the hook's expressions read as `vars.<name>`, as in `{ migrations = "db/migrations/" }`.
- `when` (String) A CEL condition the event must meet besides `match`, written bare, as in `event.inputs.query != ''`. It reads `event`, `task`, `run`, `vars` and `hook`.

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) Names the resource within its workspace, as in `core/migrations-need-a-dba`.
- `id` (String) Issued by Spotlight when the hook is created, and never changed.
- `version` (Number) Rises with every change to the hook; each write sends it back so a change made since is not overwritten.

<a id="nestedatt--match"></a>
### Nested Schema for `match`

Optional:

- `lines` (Set of String) The lines whose tasks the hook fires for, by key, as in `delivery`.
- `paths` (Set of String) Globs of the changed paths the hook fires for, as in `db/migrations/**`; only on `pull-request.opening` and `pull-request.merged`.
- `repositories` (Set of String) The repositories the hook fires for, as `owner/name`.
- `stations` (Set of String) The stations whose tasks the hook fires for, by key, as in `implementation`.
- `tools` (Set of String) The tools the hook fires for, as `integration.tool`, as in `spotlight_integration.grafana.tools["search"]`; only on `tool.using` and `tool.used`.


<a id="nestedatt--signing"></a>
### Nested Schema for `signing`

Optional:

- `oidc` (Attributes) Signs each request with a short-lived OIDC token Spotlight issues, instead of a secret. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--signing--oidc))
- `secret_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The HMAC secret Spotlight signs each request with, as Standard Webhooks sign: `whsec_` followed by 24 to 64 base64-encoded random bytes, as `"whsec_${base64encode(random_password.hook.result)}"` makes. Needed with `secret_wo_version`, and given again whenever it changes. It is sent to Spotlight and never stored in the plan or the state, so it needs Terraform 1.11 or later; change `secret_wo_version` to send it again.
- `secret_wo_version` (Number) A whole number from 1; change it whenever `secret_wo` changes, so Terraform sends the new value.

<a id="nestedatt--signing--oidc"></a>
### Nested Schema for `signing.oidc`

Required:

- `audience` (String) Who the token is for, as the endpoint checks it, as in `https://audit.acme.dev`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_hook.migrations
  identity = {
    id = "0d6f3c1e-8a52-4f7b-9c1d-5e2a7b3f9c40"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The id Spotlight issued the hook when it was created.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_hook.migrations
  id = "5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/core/migrations-need-a-dba"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A hook is imported by its workspace's id and its address, <team key>/<key>.
terraform import spotlight_hook.migrations 5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/core/migrations-need-a-dba
```
